question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?

claims.text: Explicit statements - Merrill: Merrill (inside Bank of America's GWIM) is the only one of the five whose own materials use the term. A Bank of America GWIM investor-day slide (published 2025-11-05) lays out a "Wealth Continuum" that labels "Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)" and "High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM)". The slide is a GWIM slide (Merrill plus the Private Bank) and does not itself name Merrill.

Explicit statements - Merrill: The Bank of America 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13 per the filing set; GWIM section) states that Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business provides "a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets." It does not use the words "mass affluent".

Explicit statements - Schwab: Schwab speaks of "affluent" clients and does not use "mass affluent" in the evidence. On the 4Q25 earnings call (published 2026-01-21) CEO Rick Wurster said "About one-third of new clients are affluent" and that Schwab is "winning with investors of all ages, wealth tiers, and time horizons."

Explicit statements - Schwab: On the 2Q26 call (published 2026-07-21), Wurster said 61% of affluent clients ages 25 to 44 prefer to consolidate wealth and banking relationships, and that households with $1 million to $5 million in assets using only one financial services firm "jumped 11 percentage points year-over-year to 22%".

Definition and thresholds - Merrill: In the Bank of America GWIM investor-day deck (2025-11-05), the "Mass Affluent" tier is defined as $500K - $1MM, and the next tier, High Net Worth, as $1MM - $10MM. Separately, the 2025 10-K says Merrill's advisory business focuses on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets, and a 1Q26 GWIM deck (published 2026-04-15) describes Merrill primary households as those with $250K+ in investable assets. The evidence does not reconcile the $250K and $500K lines.

Strategy and products - Schwab: At its May 2026 investor day (deck published 2026-05-14), Schwab presented a slide on growing advice share and cited "68% of affluent investors want & are willing to pay for advice". On the 2Q26 call (2026-07-21), Wurster said more retail clients seek "holistic financial advice delivered seamlessly on their terms through a combination of people and increasingly AI-enabled technology". He said Schwab is investing heavily in Schwab Wealth Advisory, including tax, trust and estate capabilities, and that its Client Promoter Score is the highest of any Schwab offer. These statements refer to affluent investors and retail clients, not to a defined mass-affluent segment.

Strategy and products - Merrill: The Bank of America 2025 10-K says Merrill Wealth Management provides "tailored solutions" through "a full set of investment management, brokerage, banking and retirement products" to clients with over $250,000 in investable assets. In the GWIM investor-day deck (2025-11-05), management said it believes "the Wealth Continuum allows us to deliver as one company" and that it has "the capabilities to deliver for every client in the way they want to be served". On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-14), the CFO cited advisor productivity, digital engagement and AI tools that "expand our capacity to deliver personalized advice at scale", and said 67% of Merrill clients have banking relationships with the firm.

Growth priorities and results - Schwab: On the 4Q25 call (2026-01-21), Wurster said about one-third of new clients are affluent. On the 2Q26 call (2026-07-21), he said that households with $1 million to $5 million in assets using only one firm rose to 22% and "we expect this to grow as more investors seek the convenience of one-stop shopping." Schwab does not report separate results for a mass-affluent segment in the evidence.

Growth priorities and results - Merrill: GWIM's 2Q26 deck (published 2026-07-14) reports about 5.4K net new $500K+ households added in Merrill in 2Q26. On the 3Q26 call (2026-10-14), the CFO said Merrill added about 4,200 net new households with at least $500,000 in assets, up 17%, and attributed this to "strong demand for advice". The $500K+ measure spans the deck's mass-affluent ($500K-$1MM) and higher tiers and is not split by tier.

adjacent.text: A Morgan Stanley trade-press item (published 2026-10-21) reports a June 2025 Cerulli Associates finding that 52% of mass-affluent participants without an advisor say their retirement savings account provider is their primary source of retirement planning guidance, and refers to a Morgan Stanley survey.
adjacent.differs_because: It is trade press relaying Cerulli research, not a statement by Morgan Stanley about its own mass-affluent clients; trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: Schwab's 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes Schwab Private Client Services for clients with $1 million to $10 million in qualifying assets and Schwab Private Wealth Services for clients with more than $10 million.
adjacent.differs_because: These are Schwab's high-wealth service tiers; they are not a definition of a mass-affluent or emerging-affluent segment.

adjacent.text: Raymond James trade press (published 2026-09-29) says its Private Wealth Advisor designation is for advisors serving high-net-worth clients, "generally defined as those with at least $5 million in investable assets".
adjacent.differs_because: This defines high net worth, not mass affluent, and is trade-press reporting, which is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: A Cerulli research release (published 2026-03-25) describes middle-market and mass-affluent households as having between $100,000 and $2 million in financial assets, a $25 trillion market of 46.9 million households. It says wealth firms have traditionally started relationships at minimums of $250,000 to more than $1 million.
adjacent.differs_because: This is an industry research definition, not any of the five firms' own definition.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley's 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) describes Wealth Management as serving "individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions" through Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace channels.
adjacent.differs_because: It describes the whole Wealth Management segment and does not mention mass-affluent clients.

adjacent.text: Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) lists initiatives targeting High Net Worth clients, Workplace (local business owners and their employees), and a new digital platform for Next Generation investors.
adjacent.differs_because: These are named target segments; none is described as mass affluent.

adjacent.text: On the 3Q26 call (published 2026-10-15), Schwab's Wurster said roughly 80% of retail assets are held by ultra-high-net-worth and high-net-worth households.
adjacent.differs_because: This describes the top wealth tiers' share of retail assets, not results for mass-affluent clients.
